description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level (undergraduate or graduate), sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV and contains total, men’s, and women’s counts for the race/ethnicity categories.

12-month instructional activity measured in credit hours and/or contact hours, reported by institution and instructional level for undergraduate and graduate activity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and the instructional-level variable EFALEVEL.

Awards and degrees conferred from July 1, 2003, through June 30, 2004, reported by 6-digit CIP program, award level, major sequence, race/ethnicity, and gender. The table includes certificates and degrees, distinguishes first versus second major, and contains total awards plus awards for men and women overall and within each of nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; no additional institution-eligibility or even/odd-year reporting restriction is stated.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL, with totals and male/female counts for full-time and part-time students.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL, with total and male/female counts for all race/ethnicity categories and full- and part-time attendance.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY; age reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2004 (even) has data where institutions reported it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE; residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2004 (even) is not an optional residence-reporting year and the table has data.

Fall enrollment counts for four-year institutions, broken down by selected major field, race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. The included fields are Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, attendance status, and EFCIPLEV.

Total entering-class counts and first-year retention rates, restricted to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data apply only to academic-year institutions; short-program institutions do not have retention data. For 2004, retention is reported as rates only, without the underlying counts needed to generate them.

Institution-level finance records for public institutions using GASB 34/35, including revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities. Each record is identified by the public institution.

Component-unit finance records for public GASB institutions whose legally separate component units use FASB. Each record is identified by the primary institution and component unit, and includes the component-unit name, general nature, assets, liabilities, and net assets; it covers component-unit financial data available for fiscal years 2001–2006.

Component-unit finance records for public GASB institutions whose legally separate component units use GASB. Each record is identified by the primary institution and component unit, and includes the component-unit name, general nature, assets, liabilities, and net assets; it covers component-unit financial data available for fiscal years 2001–2006.

Institution-level finance records for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities. Each record is identified by the institution; public GASB institutions belong in the separate GASB table.

Institution-level finance records for private for-profit institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Each record is identified by the institution and is restricted to the private for-profit sector.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for 1998 cohorts at four-year institutions and 2001 cohorts at two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity and by cohort/graduation status. Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort/graduation-status code (GRTYPE); the table includes bachelor’s-degree-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking students at four-year institutions, with bachelor’s completion milestones at 100, 125, and 150 percent of normal time.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for the 2001 cohort at less-than-2-year institutions, including students enrolled and those who completed a program or transferred out within 150 percent of normal time.

Fall 2004 staff counts broken down by occupational category, faculty and tenure status, medical school status, and full- versus part-time status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which combines occupational category, tenure status, and work status.

Fall 2004 payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- versus part-time status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, which defines the occupational and work-status category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2004 (even) may have no data for many institutions.

Fall 2004 employee counts broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender for degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees, all nondegree-granting institutions, and related administrative offices. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL, the primary-function or occupation category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2004 (even) may have no data for many institutions.

Fall 2004 full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff counts broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. The table applies to degree-granting institutions and related administrative offices with at least 15 full-time employees; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, which combines faculty/tenure status with academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2004 (even) may have no data for many institutions.

Fall 2004 full-time new-hire counts broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender; new hires are represented for the July 1 through October 31 survey-year hiring period. The table applies to degree-granting institutions and related administrative offices with at least 15 full-time employees; each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, the primary-occupation category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2004 (even) may have no data for many institutions.

Academic year 2004-05 counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and contract length (9/10-month, 11/12-month, or equated 9/10-month). Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.

Academic year 2004-05 fringe-benefit recipient counts, total expenditures, and average expenditures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each row is cataloged as uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE, the benefit-plan type.

Institution-by-survey-component response-status records, uniquely identified by institution and survey component. It covers response, nonresponse with imputation, survey applicability, parent/child multi-campus reporting, and revised-data submission status.

Institution directory records for each institution, with the institution identifier as the row key. The table distinguishes active status and Title IV participation and includes contact and web addresses plus derived institutional classifications such as control, level, highest award level, highest degree, and Carnegie classification.

Institution-level records of educational offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, and admissions information. Applicant, admission, and test-score fields apply only to institutions that do not have an open-admissions policy.

Academic-year student-charge records for institutions whose programs are primarily academic and measured in credit hours, including semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic-calendar programs. The institution is the row grain, with charges for full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate students, full-time first-professional students, and published full-time first-time undergraduate price of attendance.

Program-level student-charge records for institutions with clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, identified by institution and program. The table includes the number of programs, price of attendance for entering students in the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs.
Institution-level mission-statement records, identified by institution. Each record contains the mission statement or a web address where it is available.

Student financial aid counts and average dollar amounts for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students during July 1, 2003–June 30, 2004. The table is reported at the institution-by-aid-source/type grain and covers federal grants, state or local grants, institutional grants, and student loans; it is restricted to this undergraduate population and does not describe aid for other students.
